summary: This November 17, 2023 opinion piece argues that cities must urgently revise zoning laws to protect and expand green spaces as part of sustainable urban development. It cites examples from Oslo and Vancouver and quotes experts, officials and activists on zoning reform, incentives, community engagement and climate resilience. It concludes that green zoning should be the foundation of urban design.
one_line: An opinion piece urging cities to overhaul zoning laws to promote green spaces, supported by case studies, incentives, community input and climate resilience arguments.
key_facts: The article is dated November 17, 2023 and argues zoning laws must be revised immediately to promote urban green spaces.
Since September of 2023, numerous reports have highlighted a precipitous decline in parks, open spaces, and urban forests in metropolitan areas worldwide.
Green spaces are described as the 'lungs of a city', filtering pollutants, providing oxygen, and mitigating the heat island effect.
Nina Patel, an urban planner and sustainable development expert, said on November 5, 2023: 'Reimagining zoning is the first line of defense against urban decay.'
On September 14, 2023, Oslo implemented the 'Green Roof' mandate, requiring new buildings above a certain size to include plant life on their roofs.
Vancouver has set aside zones exclusively for parks and community gardens within its urban sprawl as part of its 'Green Zoning' policies.
Vancouver city council member David Thomson said on October 12, 2023 that Green Zoning 'doesn't stifle development. It encourages it.'
Maria Hernandez, a local government official, said on November 8, 2023 that sustainable urban development is 'akin to a puzzle' with interlocking policies from zoning to waste management.
Economist Jason Brooks, consulted on November 1, 2023, advocates tax rebates, expedited permits, and subsidies, calling the 'carrot-stick approach' powerful for adoption of Green Zoning.
Recommended community engagement tools include public surveys, participatory budgeting, and stakeholder consultations.
Activist Samantha Cho said at a rally on October 21, 2023: 'Our city, our home, our say.'
Climate scientist Dr. Emily Lau said at a symposium on October 26, 2023 that green spaces are 'indispensable assets' for climate adaptation.
Urban forestry and green roofs help cool cities and manage stormwater, reducing flood risk and the burden on drainage systems.
The broader sustainability approach includes public transit, pedestrian pathways, cycling lanes, renewable energy, greywater recycling, and sustainable waste management.
